title: C-0142's corrected 10 x 6 coupled cells, re-read at C-0140's two-length raster
verificationType: logical (an exact integer construction of the two-length raster's axial levels, station windows and census, derived from C-0140's own machinery) + in-silico (C-0142's influence surrogate and Monte Carlo dropout grading, on one common stream)
maturity: TRL 1-3. Model-consistent and traceable. NOT empirically demonstrated. The FOLDING statistics graded against are measured; the flatness is not, and the raster is a LATTICE statement.

conventions.raster: C-0140's two-length x-raster: 112 bp at effective sense 1, 108 bp at effective sense 2, first axial sign +1, unmirrored
conventions.widthReadings: row length 112 bp (every raster row's own span, C-0142's tile) and block extent 116 bp (the block's axial bounding box, the dimension SS3 is owed)
conventions.crossSection: C-0141's honeycomb: in-plane row pitch 3d/2, layer pitch d sqrt(3)/2, cell 3 sqrt(3)/4 d^2
conventions.mandate: C-0017's equality on the SUM, SS3's acceptable clause: 100 pN / 3 nm

cheapBound.attachmentPitchAcross: edgeY / rasterRows, UNCHANGED by a row-length move
cheapBound.whatItSaid: C-0140's 112 / 108 bp raster puts EVERY x-raster row of the 10 x 6 block at 112 base pairs and offsets consecutive rows axially by 4 bp. The block's extent is 116 bp = 39.44 nm only BECAUSE the rows are staggered, not because any row is longer -- so the +3.57 % width question splits into two readings, a row-faithful 112 bp and a bounding-box 116 bp, and the row-faithful one is C-0142's own tile. The face's rooting helices alternate sense EXACTLY with the raster row parity, so the station lattice is still a two-phase object. And it is not a property of the pair C-0140 selects: over all five pairs its own table carries, and at both cross-sections, every raster row spans the LARGER of the two lengths exactly and the block extent exceeds it by exactly the stagger -- so no two-length raster lengthens a row at all.

convergence.axis: CrossoverLayout.EDGE_MARGIN, the crossover-column count at the block width
convergence.note: a numerical guard is not a convergence parameter, and this axis is here because the 116 bp extent clears eleven honeycomb pitches by 0.07 nm

findings.theCheapBound: C-0140's 112 / 108 bp raster puts EVERY x-raster row of the 10 x 6 block at 112 base pairs and offsets consecutive rows axially by 4 bp. The block's extent is 116 bp = 39.44 nm only BECAUSE the rows are staggered, not because any row is longer -- so the +3.57 % width question splits into two readings, a row-faithful 112 bp and a bounding-box 116 bp, and the row-faithful one is C-0142's own tile. The face's rooting helices alternate sense EXACTLY with the raster row parity, so the station lattice is still a two-phase object. And it is not a property of the pair C-0140 selects: over all five pairs its own table carries, and at both cross-sections, every raster row spans the LARGER of the two lengths exactly and the block extent exceeds it by exactly the stagger -- so no two-length raster lengthens a row at all.
findings.theOtherCrossSection: 15 x 4 is 0 of 8 at the two-length raster's width, against 0 of 8 at C-0142's -- the direction the task asked for, and it does not move.
findings.theLatticePlacement: On the two-length station lattice at C-0142's own phase 0 / 7 bp offset, 3 of 8 cells are flat, and at the one station-saturating phase (11 / 14 bp) 3 of 8, against C-0142's 3 of 8 on the single-length lattice. The best is 1 column(s), equal springs, p90 = 0.0831416174.
findings.theStationCensus: The 21 bp ladder becomes ROW-DEPENDENT: at C-0142's own phase 0 / 7 bp offset the two-length face carries 55 stations of 60 against the uniform raster's 60, and over the whole 21-phase x 2-offset sweep exactly 1 pair(s) keep all sixty -- phase 11 at the 14 bp offset. C-0141 records that no answer of its own depends on the 7-or-14 bp offset choice; at a two-length raster that stops being true. Every graded column count (1, 2, 3, 5) is still realisable, so the raster costs stations and not paths.
findings.theDecomposition: The two effects of a +3.57 % axial extent are OPPOSED and the numerical guard picks which wins. At a MATCHED eleven crossover columns the wider tile is worse -- the uncoupled reference goes 0.0240648102 to 0.0252615047 -- and the TWELFTH crossover column the standing guard admits takes it to 0.0231299291, below the 112 bp reading. The coupled flat count runs 4 of 8 at 112 bp, 3 of 8 at 116 bp on eleven columns and 6 of 8 on twelve -- and every raster ROW is 112 bp, so eleven is the count a row can carry and twelve is the count the BOUNDING BOX admits.
findings.theVerdict: Of 8 10 x 6 coupled cells re-read at the two-length raster's bounding-box width at the measured f = 0.30, 6 are flat at the 90th percentile against 4 of 8 at C-0142's 112 bp width. At the band's adverse low end f = 0.26 it is 4 of 8. The best block-width cell is 1 column(s), equal springs, p90 = 0.0662801686 against C-0142's 0.0680677948 at the same cell.
findings.theWidthCost: Read PER REALISATION on the shared stream, the block width costs the 10 x 6 tile a median ratio of 0.873618 to 1.02386, against a ratio of 90th percentiles of 0.893271 to 1.03315. CLAUDE.md: a ratio of two ORDER STATISTICS is not the order statistic of the ratio.
findings.theGuard: A +3.57 % axial extent clears eleven honeycomb crossover pitches by 0.07 nm, so the column count is 12 at the standing guard and 11 at half a base-pair rise. Swept: the flat cell set is DIFFERENT at the two guards, and the worst cell moves 0.066 relative.

validity: The raster is a LATTICE statement (C-0140): no folded object is measured, and the two-length assignment is a design this repository derives rather than one anybody has built.

The two ENDS of the scaffold path carry no defined turn sense (C-0140), so their length is free. 10 x 6's face is clear of both; 15 x 4's row 14 face helix IS the path terminus and its sense is extrapolated from the row parity.
The block extent is taken over the INTERIOR helices, which is C-0140's own convention; the two terminal helices could extend it further.

The tile is a SMEARED equivalent sheet with ONE lengthX, so the 4 bp axial STAGGER between consecutive raster rows is not representable at all -- which is exactly why both width readings are carried and neither is preferred.

The dropout statistics are measured on a SINGLE-LAYER Rothemund rectangle; only the PROFILE transfers, in nm, and the wider tile changes the perimeter-to-area ratio again. C-0109's assumption, inherited.
The mandate is read at SS3's ACCEPTABLE clause (100 pN / 3 nm).
Two distributions only -- equal and C-0058's rim rule.
C-0022's collar is read unchanged at the wider aspect ratio; C-0123's question is reopened again rather than answered.
Kirchhoff is not safe at these thicknesses (C-0109, C-0120): every D_par is an upper bound.
openQuestions: Which of the two width readings a folded block is owed against SS3 -- the bounding box the object occupies or the row length its beams carry. Nothing here settles it, and the two differ by 3.57 %.
What the 4 bp inter-row axial STAGGER costs a flatness model that can represent it; a single-lengthX grillage cannot.
Which ladder phase and which of the two inter-row offsets a caDNAno honeycomb carries, which now decides a station COUNT and not only a position.
Whether C-0089's percentile descent recovers any cell the two-length raster loses.
